svg.title: Figure 3. A real clamp is not perfectly fixed
svg.desc: Two panels. (a) A cantilever held by a clamp drawn as a rotational spring of stiffness k. With a rigid clamp the beam leaves the wall horizontally; with a flexible clamp the wall end rotates by an angle equal to the wall moment divided by k, and the whole beam tilts further down. (b) The prop reaction of a propped cantilever against the clamp flexibility EI over k L on a logarithmic axis: with a central load it rises from five sixteenths of P for a rigid clamp to one half of P when the clamp becomes a pin; under a uniform load it rises from three eighths of w L to one half.
